definition: the expanse of air above the earth, seen from the ground
hook: English took the word sky from the Vikings, and it meant the thing in the way of it.
modernAnchor: Blue overhead, a plane crossing it, nothing at all in the way. We call it the sky.
journey: Old Norse ský meant cloud, and it came into English around 1200 with the Scandinavian settlers.
English already had its own words for the heavens. What it borrowed from Norse was the word for the grey stuff crossing them.
For a long stretch of Middle English, sky meant cloud and little else. When a writer said the skies, he meant the clouds.
Then the word drifted upward, past the thing it named, and settled on the whole open expanse behind it.
